newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Hasina vows to reduce hunger, blasts opponents.
newsitem.headline: Hasina vows to reduce hunger, blasts opponents.

text.p: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday vowed Bangladesh would make every effort to do its part to meet the World Food Summit's goal of halving the number of hungry people in the world by 2015.
"We have endorsed the Plan of Action of the Rome summit and we will do our best to attain the target," Hasina told a news conference in Dhaka on her return from the Italian capital.
She said Bangladesh was facing a severe food crisis, and that "nearly 86 percent of the country's (nearly 120 million) people cannot arrange nutritious meals even twice a day".
"Children are dying of malnutrition. The chief aim of my government is to get those hungry people food... (and) we are working day and night for that," the prime minister said.
Hasina said she had formed a team of experts to advise the government on agriculture.
The U.N. Food & Agriculture Organisation has announced a 35 percent increase in technical assistance to Bangladesh, she said without giving details.
But she warned that the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) was "sabotaging" the government's development efforts by stirring up political unrest.
"It's unfortunate the way the opposition is behaving," Hasina said, referring to a boycott of parliament by the BNP.
BNP legislators, led by the party's chief and former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, walked out on November 10.
They alleged that the ruling Awami League was not allowing opposition legislators to express their views on matters of national interest.
The BNP also alleged that Hasina's government had detained over 500 BNP workers and activists, and said it would continue the boycott until they were freed.
Hasina said on Tuesday that there have been no politically motivated arrests during her nearly five months of rule.
"We have arrested only criminals and terrorists. What can we do if some of them also belong to a political party. Criminals must face the consequences," she said.
Hasina said the BNP was holding up the nation's development.
"In a short time we have spruced up the image of the country in the outside world. Now that foreign investors have started responding, they (the BNP) are out to negate it," she said.
Khaleda has launched an attack on the government and has asked her followers to prepare for a campaign to topple it.
At BNP rallies earlier this month, Khaleda said the government was "subservient to Indian interests", putting the nation's independence and sovereignty in peril.
